land.text: the Breton land, passing unchanged from Cliopatria's Breton Kingdoms row (ends 824) to its Kingdom of Brittany row (starts 825) on the same 24,213 km2 outline

predecessors.note: The breton-kingdoms dossier records the same hand-over at confidence 1; the Kingdom of Brittany page lists the rulers Morman (814-818) and Wihomarc (822-825) and has no break in 825.

land.text: Brittany under Alan II, 'duke of Brittany' after the 939 reconquest

successors.note: The page's ruler list has Alan II reconquering Brittany in 939 and becoming duke; in 942 he 'paid tribute as duke of Brittany to king Louis IV'. Cliopatria's Duchy of Brittany row starts in 947, so 940-946 are drawn by nobody in Cliopatria; the duchy dossier (eu-10) should start in 939 or 940. The infobox also lists the Duchy of Normandy and 'Viking Upper Brittany' as successors, without dates. The Avranchin and the Cotentin passed to the Duchy of Normandy in 933 (ledger loss 933).

capitals.name: Vannes
capitals.note: Unverified: none of the five pages names a capital (the Kingdom of Brittany infobox gives none; the Erispoe page says only that 'his power base was in the Vannetais and southeast Brittany'). Vannes is the seat the pages hint at: Nominoe 'count of Vannes' (Kingdom page), Alan I 'succeeded his brother Pascweten in Vannes' (Alan I page). Follow-up after review (eu-07-d): the Nominoe page has two charters calling Nominoe 'Count of Vannes' (date uncertain, 819 to 834); the Vannes page says Vannes was the duchy's capital in the 14th and 15th centuries and is silent on the 9th. Still unverified.

rulers.name: Wihomarc
rulers.note: Led a rebellion against Frankish rule (822-825). The page lists no ruler for 826-840. Reign 822-825 on the page; 'from' clipped to the dossier's start year (reviewer eu-07-d).

rulers.name: Nominoe
rulers.title: duke (count of Vannes)
rulers.note: Defeated Frankish troops at Ballon (845); took the Frankish garrisons of Rennes and Nantes in 851.

rulers.name: Erispoe
rulers.title: king (royal title and regalia from Charles the Bald, 851)
rulers.note: Assassinated in November 857 by his cousin Salomon (Erispoe page).

rulers.name: Salomon
rulers.title: king (styled so from 868, 'not king in any official capacity')
rulers.note: Killed by Pascweten, Gurvand and Wigo in 874 (Salomon page).

rulers.name: Gurvand
rulers.title: rival claimant
rulers.note: The page gives no reign dates; both rivals died in 876.

rulers.name: Pascweten
rulers.title: rival claimant
rulers.note: Alan I succeeded his brother Pascweten in Vannes in mid-876 (Alan I page).

rulers.name: Alan I
rulers.title: king (rex Brittaniae; with Judicael to 888)
rulers.note: Sole ruler after Judicael died at Questembert in 888 or 889; 'only King of Brittany to hold that title by a grant of the Emperor'.

rulers.name: Gourmaelon
rulers.title: count of Cornouaille, did not claim the title of king
rulers.note: Seized the throne in the disputed succession; 'Brittany was soon overrun by Vikings'.

rulers.name: Alan II (Alan Twistedbeard)
rulers.title: last ruler of the infobox list; duke after 939
rulers.note: Landed in 935 and recovered most of Brittany by 937; no ruler is listed for 913-937 (Norse occupation from 919).

keyframe_review.note: 24,213 km2, drawn 825-859: the Breton core without Rennes, Nantes and Retz. Right for 825-850 only: the Frankish counties of Rennes and Nantes and the Pays de Retz came to the Bretons in 851 ('Frankish garrisons left in the previous year in Rennes and Nantes capitulated to Nominoe', Treaty of Angers, September 851), so the new keyframe kingdom-of-brittany_851 takes over from 851. The page gives no infobox area and no boundary for 825-850. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026: from/to (825, 850) set as the entry's own text says (fx-48 handoff), so it no longer overlaps the next keyframe]

correction.text: the Breton core as drawn, for 825-850 only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 851-862: Cliopatria dates the Rennes-Nantes-Retz addition to 860, nine years late. The Jengland page: after the victory of 22 August 851 'Charles recognized the authority of Breton rulers over the areas around Rennes, Nantes, and Pays de Retz', formerly the Frankish 'Breton March'; the Erispoe page: invested with the counties of Rennes and Nantes and the Pays de Retz, 'detached from the County of Poitou'. Cliopatria's 860 outline less its 15 cells in Mayenne and Maine-et-Loire (western Anjou, dated 863 by the Salomon page). 149 cells less 15 = 134 cells.

correction.text: the Breton core with the counties of Rennes and Nantes and the Pays de Retz

keyframe_review.note: 40,598 km2, drawn 860-865: the 851 land plus 15 cells in Mayenne and Maine-et-Loire. The Salomon page: in 852 he held Rennes, Nantes and Retz 'as a third of Brittany, held from Charles in fee' and Nantes 'passed to Robert the Strong at the end of his tenure' in 860 (the page does not say Brittany lost it); the Anjou cells come from the 863 peace at Entrammes. So 860-862 is the 851 keyframe and 863-865 the 866 outline; this shape is superseded.

correction.text: for 860-862 the shape without western Anjou; from 863 see kingdom-of-brittany_863

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 863-866: Cliopatria's 866 outline (41,556 km2) applies from 863. The Salomon page: 863 'Charles marched on Brittany but stopped near Entrammes and negotiated a peace. Western Anjou was recognised as part of Brittany, and Salomon was granted the lay abbacy of Saint-Aubin in Angers.' Cliopatria draws only 17 cells of Mayenne and Maine-et-Loire.

correction.text: the Breton land with western Anjou after Entrammes

keyframe_review.note: 41,556 km2, drawn 866-869: right for 863-866 only (new keyframe 863); the next outline applies from 867. Robert the Strong fell at Brissarthe in 866 fighting Vikings allied with the Bretons (same page).

New keyframe, 867-869: Cliopatria dates Avranches and Coutances to 870, three years late. The Salomon page: '867: Salomon was granted the counties of Avranches and Coutances ... Pascweten negotiated a peace at Compiegne in August'; the Kingdom of Brittany page has Charles giving away 'the provinces of Cotentin (863) and Maine (867)', which disagrees on names and years; the shape (19 cells in Manche) follows the Salomon page, as the west-franks dossier does.

correction.text: the Breton land with Avranches and Coutances

keyframe_review.note: 47,425 km2, 870-879, the largest outline. The Alan I page: Alan 'ruled not only the Breton territories of Leon, Domnonee, Cornouaille and the Vannetais but also the Frankish counties of Rennes, Nantes, Coutances and Avranches, as well as the western parts of Poitou (Retz) and Anjou. In the east his rule extended as far as the river Vire'; 'Brittany's geographic territory was never as extended as in Alan I's time'. The 874-876 civil war after Salomon's murder moved no border on the pages.

45,759 km2, 880-881: 5 cells less than 870 in Loire-Atlantique. The Alan I page notes Fulk I of Anjou 'disputed control of the Nantais' with Alan (undated) and contacts with Nantes in 886; no page dates a loss, so the outline stands within the precision of the era.
45,804 km2, 882-887: one cell more than 880; nothing on the pages. Charles the Fat's succession in West Francia in 884 'does not seem' to have reached Brittany (Alan I page).
45,759 km2, 888-895: Judicael died at Questembert in 888 or 889 and Alan became sole ruler; in 890 Alan beat the Vikings at Saint-Lo. No border moves.
45,804 km2, 896-910: the same outline; Alan I died in 907 and 'Brittany was soon overrun by Vikings', which the page does not date; the shape stays whole to 918.
45,804 km2, drawn 911-921: right for 911-918 only. The Kingdom of Brittany page: 'From 919, Brittany was completely occupied by the Norsemen'; the next two keyframes carry 919-939.

New keyframe, 919-932: Cliopatria's row ends in 921 but the page has Brittany 'completely occupied by the Norsemen' from 919; the Alan I page has the Vikings holding it 'until 936', when Alan II returned from exile (the Kingdom page: landed 935, 'recovered most of Brittany' by 937; the Alan II page: occupation 'from 907 to about 939', landing at Dol in 936). The land is Norse-occupied (hatched), not a Norse state: Cliopatria's Viking settlements row draws Normandy and the Loire from 922. The shape holds to 932: in 933 the Avranchin and the Cotentin go to Normandy (ledger loss 933; keyframe 933). Shortened from 936 after review (eu-07-d).

correction.text: Brittany as one hatched occupied land

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 933-936: the Avranchin and the Cotentin (the 22 cells of the 867 gain, Avranches and Coutances) leave Brittany. Duchy of Normandy page: William Longsword 'supported Rudolph and in 933 in return was granted Avranchin and the heavily Norse Cotentin', lands that 'were in practice outside effective Carolingian control and so had to be forcibly taken from the Duchy of Brittany'. The rest of the 911 outline stays Norse-occupied until Alan II's return. The gazetteer gives 22 cells for this region (the reviewer counted 29 for 911 minus 866; the ledger's 867 gain uses the same 22-cell region). Added after review (eu-07-d).

minus.text: Avranchin and the heavily Norse Cotentin

correction.text: Brittany as one hatched occupied land without the Avranchin and the Cotentin, which William Longsword received in 933

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 937-939: 'By 937, he had recovered most of Brittany and the Norsemen retreated to their stronghold of Trans-la-Foret'; 'In 939, a combined army of Frankish and Breton soldiers attacked the fortress' (key battle 1 August 939). The outline is the 911 shape without the Avranchin and the Cotentin, which Normandy received in 933 and Brittany did not recover (Duchy of Normandy page; the Alan II page has Alan 'renounced the Cotentin, Avranchin and Mayenne' and paid homage to Louis IV in 942), apart from the stronghold, which the page does not locate. Corrected after review (eu-07-d): the first version kept the whole 911 outline.

minus.text: Avranchin and the heavily Norse Cotentin

correction.text: Brittany under Alan II with the Norse stronghold at Trans-la-Foret, without the Avranchin and the Cotentin

ledger.note: 825: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Brittany begins on the Breton core. The page's ruler list has Wihomarc 822-825, who 'led a rebellion against Frankish rule', then no ruler until Nominoe in 841, and calls the realm a 'vassal state of the Frankish Empire'; no page opened dates a founding, so the year is Cliopatria's, bridging from the breton-kingdoms row (ends 824). Follow-up after review (eu-07-d): the Nominoe page (opened as 'Nominoe'; the percent-encoded title failed to load) says Nominoe was 'probably' appointed 'to rule the Bretons' at the general assembly of May 831 at Ingelheim, that his title Count of Vannes is dated between 819 and 834, and that he was 'the first Duke of Brittany from 846'; no sentence of it is dated 825. The year stays Cliopatria's, at confidence 1.

region.text: the Breton lands of Leon, Domnonee, Cornouaille and the Vannetais

ledger.note: 850: the Bretons seize the Frankish Breton March. 'In 850, the Bretons briefly occupied the Frankish Breton March'; the Jengland page adds that Nominoe 'resumed his offensive against the Franks' in 849.

region.text: the Frankish Breton March: Rennes, Nantes and Retz

ledger.note: 851: Jengland and Angers end the contest. 'The Battle of Jengland took place on 22 August 851'; 'The Bretons were victorious, leading to the signing of the Treaty of Angers in September 851.'

851: Erispoe wins Rennes, Nantes and Retz at Angers and a royal title. 'Charles recognized the authority of Breton rulers over the areas around Rennes, Nantes, and Pays de Retz'; 'In September, Erispoe submitted to Charles as Emperor, while receiving the title of king in return', in principle still subject to him. The west-franks dossier records the matching loss.

region.text: the areas around Rennes, Nantes and the Pays de Retz

ledger.note: 863: Salomon's peace at Entrammes recognises western Anjou as Breton. 'Charles marched on Brittany but stopped near Entrammes and negotiated a peace. Western Anjou was recognised as part of Brittany'; Salomon commended himself to Charles and paid tribute. The 17 cells (Mayenne, Maine-et-Loire) are Cliopatria's 866 addition; the page names no town but Angers (Saint-Aubin).

867: Salomon is granted Avranches and Coutances. 'Salomon was granted the counties of Avranches and Coutances'; Charles marched on Brittany again and Pascweten made peace at Compiegne in August. The west-franks dossier records the matching loss. The Kingdom of Brittany page has instead 'Cotentin (863) and Maine (867)'.

region.text: the counties of Avranches and Coutances (the Cotentin)

ledger.note: 919: the Norsemen occupy Brittany. 'From 919, Brittany was completely occupied by the Norsemen.' The Alan I page: after Alan I's death in 907 'Brittany was soon overrun by Vikings'. The Alan II page has an occupation 'from 907 to about 939'; the year 919 is the Kingdom of Brittany page's, and the 911 shape stays whole for 911-918.

region.text: Avranchin and the heavily Norse Cotentin

ledger.note: 933: the Avranchin and the Cotentin go to Normandy. William Longsword 'supported Rudolph and in 933 in return was granted Avranchin and the heavily Norse Cotentin', lands that 'were in practice outside effective Carolingian control and so had to be forcibly taken from the Duchy of Brittany' (Duchy of Normandy page; the sentence does not name the grantor, the context is King Rudolph). Brittany does not recover them: the Alan II page has Alan 'renounced the Cotentin, Avranchin and Mayenne and paid homage to Louis IV in 942' (second page; Mayenne is also named there, but no page dates its loss and it stays in the shape to 939). The region is the 22 cells of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Brittany shape of 870 inside West Franks 866, the 867 gain (Avranches and Coutances). The Kingdom of Brittany infobox lists the Duchy of Normandy among the successors. Added after review (eu-07-d).

937: Alan II recovers Brittany. 'In 935, Alan Twistedbeard disembarked once more on the shores of Brittany in order to reconquer his domain. By 937, he had recovered most of Brittany and the Norsemen retreated to their stronghold of Trans-la-Foret.' The Alan I page has the Vikings holding Brittany 'until 936'. The region leaves out the Avranchin and the Cotentin, which went to Normandy in 933 (ledger loss 933) and are not part of the recovered land; the Alan II page: 'By 937 Alan was master of most of Brittany, having forced the Norsemen back to the Loire' and landing at Dol in 936.

minus.text: Avranchin and the heavily Norse Cotentin

ledger.note: 939: the kingdom gives way to the duchy. 'In 939, a combined army of Frankish and Breton soldiers attacked the fortress' of Trans-la-Foret (1 August 939); Alan II is the last ruler of the page's list (reconquered Brittany in 939 and became duke), and in 942 he 'paid tribute as duke of Brittany to king Louis IV'. The month is the infobox's date of the battle.

minus.text: Avranchin and the heavily Norse Cotentin

wars.name: Nominoe's and Erispoe's wars against Charles the Bald

zones.text: the Breton March: Rennes, Nantes, Retz

wars.outcome: Nominoe beat Frankish troops at Ballon (845), resumed the offensive in 849, occupied the Breton March in 850 and took the garrisons of Rennes and Nantes in 851; Erispoe won at Jengland on 22 August 851 and the Treaty of Angers (September 851) gave him Rennes, Nantes and Retz and a royal title.
wars.note: The Jengland page does not say Nominoe died in 851 and does not call the result independence.

wars.name: Salomon's wars with Charles the Bald
wars.outcome: Entrammes (863) recognised western Anjou as Breton; Compiegne (August 867) brought the counties of Avranches and Coutances; in 868 Charles gave Salomon regalia. Robert the Strong died at Brissarthe in 866 fighting Bretons and their Viking allies.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Brittany page dates Cotentin to 863 and Maine to 867.

wars.name: Breton civil war after Salomon's murder
wars.outcome: Pascweten, Gurvand and Wigo killed Salomon in 874; civil war until 876, when Pascweten and Gurvand died and Alan I took power. No border moved on the pages.
wars.note: Alan I contended with Judicael of Poher until they made peace against the Vikings (Alan I page).

wars.name: Alan I's wars against the Vikings
wars.outcome: Judicael died at Questembert in 888 or 889; Alan defeated the Vikings at Saint-Lo in 890. No border moved.
wars.note: Fulk I of Anjou disputed the Nantais with Alan (undated).

wars.name: Norse occupation and reconquest of Brittany
wars.outcome: Brittany completely occupied by the Norsemen from 919; Alan II landed in 935, had recovered most of Brittany by 937, and a Frankish-Breton army attacked the Norse fortress of Trans-la-Foret in 939; he became duke.
wars.note: The Alan I page dates the return of Alan II to 936.

certainty.note: The Breton marches against the Franks are approximate; no page gives a boundary.

The Angers settlement (851) and the peaces of Entrammes (863) and Compiegne (867) name counties (Rennes, Nantes, Retz, western Anjou, Avranches, Coutances), not survey lines, so they stay soft; the Vire is named as the eastern limit under Alan I (Alan I page).

notes: Kingdom of Brittany (eu-07-d), five pages (Kingdom of Brittany, Salomon of Brittany, Battle of Jengland, Alan I King of Brittany, Erispoe), the whole budget. No page gives an area or a capital; the Vannes capital is unverified. Cliopatria rows. (1) The three additions (Rennes-Nantes-Retz 860, western Anjou 866, Avranches-Coutances 870) are each 3 to 9 years later than the pages (851, 863, 867); new keyframes kingdom-of-brittany_851, _863 and _867 carry them and the 825, 860 and 866 shapes are marked adjust. (2) 880-896 shapes differ by 1 to 5 cells and are ok. (3) The row ends in 921 but the pages have Brittany Norse-occupied from 919 to 936/937 and the duchy from 939; the 911 shape is cut to 918 and new keyframes 919 (to 932), 933 (to 936) and 937 carry the occupation, the 933 loss of the Avranchin and the Cotentin to Normandy (Duchy of Normandy page, added after the review) and the reconquest; the end is 939, so the Duchy of Brittany dossier (Cliopatria starts 947) should start 939 or 940. Not settled. The Kingdom of Brittany page dates Cotentin to 863 and Maine to 867 where the Salomon page has Avranches and Coutances in 867 and western Anjou in 863; Rennes, Nantes and Retz are 851 on the Jengland and Erispoe pages but 852 and 'a third of Brittany' on the Salomon page. The page gives nothing on 826-840 or 913-934. The Breton lands are drawn as sovereign by Cliopatria while the page calls the realm a vassal state of the Frankish Empire (the Frankish side: west-franks dossier records only the 851 loss); no vassal events are recorded. Counterparts: viking-settlements (Cliopatria row 793-1332) is used for the Norse occupation; duchy-of-brittany is eu-10's. Gazetteer: all names used resolve. Repair after the review (eu-07-d): four more pages opened (Duchy of Normandy, Alan II Duke of Brittany, Nominoe, Vannes), over the budget; the Viking occupation of Brittany page failed to load (url_not_found), and Nomino%C3%AB failed but Nominoe loaded. Added: ledger loss 933 (counterpart duchy-of-normandy, confidence 3) with the Avranchin and the Cotentin, keyframes 919 (to 932), 933 and 937 and the 937 occupation_end and 939 dissolve regions without them; the ruler Wihomarc is clipped to 825 (reviewer). Disagreements: the reviewer counted 29 cells for the 911 shape minus the 866 shape; the gazetteer gives 22 cells for the region used (870 shape inside West Franks 866), 23 for 911 minus 866; the 22-cell region is the one the 867 gain already uses. The Alan II page has the occupation 'from 907 to about 939', the Kingdom of Brittany page 919 (kept); Alan II landed at Dol in 936 (Alan II page) or 935 (Kingdom page). The Alan II page also has Alan renouncing Mayenne in 942; no page dates its loss, so western Anjou stays in the shape to 939. Thin items: the 825 founding is Cliopatria's (the Nominoe page has May 831 for his appointment and nothing for 825; confidence 1 stays); Vannes stays unverified; no page for 826-840 or 913-918 found (the Viking occupation page failed). The duchy-of-normandy dossier (Cliopatria row 922-1071) does not exist yet and should carry the matching gain in 933.
